commit_message:
aacenc_tns: tune and reduce artifacts

There are a couple of major changes here:

1. Start using TNS coefficient compression.
2. Start using 3 bits per coefficient maximum for short windows.
The bits we save from these 2 changes seem to make a nice impact on the
rest of the file/windows.

3. Remove special case gain checking for short windows.
4. Modify the coefficient loop to support up to 3 windows.
The additional restrictions on TNS were something that was no in the
specifications and furthermore restricting TNS to only low energy short
windows was done to compensate for bugs elsewhere in the code.

Overall, the improvements here reduce crackling artifacts heard in very
noisy tracks.

Signed-off-by: Rostislav Pehlivanov <atomnuker@gmail.com>

findings.title: Stack buffer overflow via out-of-bounds access on en[2] array when n_filt=3
findings.message: The array `en` is declared as `float en[2]` (2 elements, indices 0 and 1), but the loop `for (g = 0; g < tns->n_filt[w]; g++)` can iterate with g=0, 1, 2 when `n_filt[w]` is set to 3 (which happens when `!is8 && order == TNS_MAX_ORDER`, i.e., AAC Main profile with long windows). Inside the loop, the expression `en[g] < en[!g]` accesses `en[2]` when g=2, which is a stack-buffer-overflow read past the end of the 2-element array. The `!g` expression also only ever evaluates to 0 or 1, so the comparison is semantically wrong for g=2 as well. An attacker can trigger this by encoding audio with the AAC Main profile (`-profile:a aac_main` or `-aac_pred true`).
findings.suggestion: Expand the `en` array to accommodate 3-filter cases (e.g., `float en[4]`) and compute energy measurements across three regions instead of two. Also change `en[g] < en[!g]` to `en[g] < en[g + 1]` so the direction comparison is meaningful for all filter indices.

ground_truth.root_cause: The commit d55f83de merged separate 1-filter and 2-filter code paths into a single unified loop that supports up to 3 filters, but failed to expand the `en[2]` energy measurement array to accommodate 3-filter access. The expression `en[g] < en[!g]` was designed for at most g=1 (2 filters), but with g=2 (3 filters), it reads past the end of the stack-allocated array.
